title: The Antigonus Family’s Notebook
briefing:
Three people read a black hardcover notebook and three people died in the small hours of the twenty-eighth of June. Naya, drowned in a basin of water in a locked room. Welch McGovern, at his own desk with the door bolted on the inside and no mark on him anywhere.

And you, who put a revolver against your own head, wrote that everyone dies including me, and got up again.

McGovern bought the notebook in May — Ancient Feysac, a family hand, and a grade the Church does not put in writing — and asked two friends to help him read it. It is not in his rooms now.

Captain Smith wants it back before whoever else is looking for it finds it. He is giving the file to the civilian staffer whose own name is already in it.

objectives.text: Establish that nobody came in or out
Work out where the notebook went
Find out who is holding it now

clues.title: The door was bolted from within
clues.text: A heavy iron bolt, thrown across and still in its housing when the police took the frame off. No trick of string throws that from the landing.

clues.title: The shutters were nailed shut
clues.text: Every window shuttered and nailed from the inside, and the nail heads are bright. He did it that week, and he did it himself.

clues.title: No wound, and no poison
clues.text: No mark on him at all. The police surgeon looked twice because he did not believe the first look, and then wrote heart failure because the form has a line for it and none for this.

clues.title: His watch stopped at 11:47
clues.text: Wound, undamaged, and stopped — not run down. The mainspring still has a day in it. Naya’s clock stopped in the same hour, three streets away, and so did the one on your own shelf.

clues.title: Two cups, and only one drunk from
clues.text: Set out on the desk, both poured, one cold and full. He had company that evening, and the company did not stay to drink.

clues.title: A page cut out of the transcription
clues.text: He was copying the notebook out longhand, bound in his own stitching, in a hand that gets worse by the page. One leaf has been taken close to the sewing with a blade, and the leaf before it ends mid-ritual.

clues.title: The book’s place on the shelf is empty
clues.text: A gap the width of a hardcover, and no dust in it, on a shelf that has dust everywhere else. Whatever stood there stood there until very recently.

clues.title: A parcel receipt, dated the twenty-eighth
clues.text: Tingen postal office, the counter that opens at six in the morning. One parcel, book rate, paid in coin. Half a day after three people stopped breathing, somebody was queueing to send a book across town.

clues.title: The receipt is in your own hand
clues.text:
The loops on the address are yours. Not the dead man’s, not a clerk’s — yours, from the hand of a body you have been wearing for eight days and did not have that morning.

You were awake before dawn on the twenty-eighth, and you have no memory of it whatsoever.

clues.title: His money was not touched
clues.text: Eleven pounds and some silver in an unlocked box on the shelf, in plain sight a yard from the body. Whoever took the notebook wanted the notebook.

clues.title: Something clings to the plumb
clues.text:
A copper weight on a waxed thread, lying where it fell. To an ordinary eye, a curiosity. To yours, it is still faintly warm in a way that has nothing to do with the fire, and it is still pointed at the chair.

This is what he divined with. This is the instrument, not the cause.

clues.title: The room remembers being afraid
clues.text: Not his fear. Fear does not print itself on plaster from one man sitting quietly in a chair. This is the shape of something that was read aloud and then arrived, and the print of it goes up the wall and stops at the ceiling like smoke that had somewhere to be.

clues.title: Franky saw you go out before light
clues.text:
Your landlord was up with a bad tooth and heard your door. Half past five, no lamp, a parcel under your arm, and back inside a quarter of an hour later.

He tells you this apologetically, as though you might be embarrassed to have forgotten it.

clues.title: The police put it at midnight
clues.text: Sergeant Gorman’s report has the surgeon putting death near midnight and the file closed as three unconnected misadventures, because the alternative is a form the Awwa County Police do not keep.

clues.title: The bell rang eleven
clues.text: Two neighbours heard it from the landing and both are certain, and both say McGovern’s lamp was still lit after it, and that he was reading aloud in a language neither of them has ever heard.

clues.title: Hanass sold him the book in May
clues.text: For four pounds, which is a great deal for a water-stained notebook and nothing at all for what it is. He will tell you the price, the date, and the weather. He will not tell you who consigned it to him.

clues.title: The parcel went to Ray Bieber
clues.text: Number nine, Cobble Yard, off the Tussock: a warehouse clerk with a room over the counting house. You have never met him. You addressed a parcel to him in the dark, six days ago, and paid book rate.

clues.title: Bieber has not been out in six days
clues.text: He signed for the parcel, sent word he was ill, and has not been seen since. His landlady has stopped knocking. She says the room has gone quiet in a way a quiet room does not, and she says it standing well back from the stairs.

clues.title: Somebody in paint is asking after it
clues.text:
Quill of Alzuhod is putting money about for a black hardcover notebook, on behalf of a client he will describe only by his manners. A man in white face paint has been seen twice on the Tussock, both times looking at the same warehouse.

Smith writes two words in his notebook and turns it face down: Secret Order.

deductions.title: Nothing came in, and nothing went out
deductions.text: Door bolted, shutters nailed from within, the money untouched a yard from the body. Every opening was fastened by the man inside it. There was no murderer in these rooms, because there was no room for one.

deductions.title: The book did it, and the reading was the door
deductions.text: No wound, no poison, and a room printed with a terror that no single frightened man could leave behind. The plumb is still warm and still pointing at the chair. Three people read it aloud; three people died in the same hour; the instrument was the reading itself.

deductions.title: They went together, at a quarter to midnight
deductions.text: A watch stopped at 11:47, a clock stopped in the same hour three streets away, a bell at eleven with the lamp still lit after it. Not one death and then another. One hour, and everyone who had read it.

deductions.title: The notebook left the rooms that night
deductions.text: A gap on the shelf with no dust in it, a leaf cut out of the transcription close to the sewing, and eleven pounds sitting untouched beside a dead man. Somebody carried the book out and took nothing else.

deductions.title: You posted it yourself, before it was light
deductions.text:
The receipt is in your handwriting. Your landlord heard your door at half past five with a parcel under your arm. You have no memory of any of it, and the hand that wrote the address is the hand you are holding the receipt with.

Whatever finished with McGovern that night was not finished with you.

deductions.title: Ray Bieber has had it for six days
deductions.text: Addressed to a warehouse clerk you have never met, signed for, and then nothing: no work, no errands, no door answered. The book has had a reader to itself for the better part of a week.

deductions.title: You are not the only one looking
deductions.text: A fence buying blind for a client with manners, a man in white paint watching the same warehouse twice, and a dealer who will name a price but not a consignor. Somebody has been a step behind this book since May, and they are no longer bothering to be discreet.

resolutions.label: Go in with the team, and bring the notebook out
resolutions.summary: The whole account, in the order a report wants it: the sealed rooms, the parcel in your own hand, the address on the Tussock, and the black hardcover book itself.
resolutions.epilogue:
You lay it out for Dunn Smith in the order a report wants it, and he listens with his eyes shut and does not write a word. At the end he says the notebook’s grade before you have finished describing the binding.

Old Neil seals it in lead and lime and signs it into the Church’s cupboard, and is quiet for the rest of the evening, which nobody here has seen before. Leonard says something about a drink and nobody answers him.

On the stairs, not looking at you, Smith says that three people read that book and three people died, and that the file has four names in it. Then he says goodnight.

resolutions.label: Give them the address and go in hard
resolutions.summary: Enough of it to justify a raid, and not enough to know what is waiting in the warehouse.
resolutions.epilogue:
It is done in eleven minutes and two of them are spent on the door. What comes up off the warehouse floor is not a clerk any more, and the thing that stops it is Daly Simone, standing in the air with her hands full of somebody else’s night.

The notebook is under the wreckage, unmarked, exactly as heavy as a book. Smith takes it in a lead case without looking at it and tells you to write the report at home, tomorrow, when you have slept.

resolutions.label: Hand the address to Smith and stay outside
resolutions.summary: The trail as far as Cobble Yard, and the Nighthawks to walk the last of it without you.
resolutions.epilogue:
They go in without you, which is what a probationer is for. Old Neil comes back with a burn along one sleeve and the notebook in a lead case, and tells you, kindly, that you would not have enjoyed it.

Smith reads your file twice. It has everything in it except the part where you were there.

resolutions.label: Trade the notebook for the name of the rung above you
resolutions.summary: A man in white paint has an offer, and nobody at the Company need ever hear it.
resolutions.epilogue:
He says the word as though handing you a coat: Clown. Sequence 8 of your own pathway, which the Church would have made you earn twice over and told you late.

Then he takes the notebook, and the paint on his face does not move when he smiles, and he says he looks forward to the next time.

You write a report that is true in every particular and answers no question anyone asked. Smith reads it twice, says nothing at all, and does not put it in the cupboard.

resolutions.label: Report that you could not close it
resolutions.summary: The rooms, the deaths, and a book nobody can account for.
resolutions.epilogue:
Smith does not take it badly, which is worse. He files it open, writes a line about the parcel you cannot explain, and tells you to go home and eat something.

Somewhere on the Tussock, a room that has gone quiet stays quiet.

leads.label: Match the receipt against the postal ledger
leads.description: The counter that opens at six keeps its own book, and a clerk who was on that morning keeps a better one.
leads.successText: The ledger has it in two lines: book rate, paid in coin, half past five, addressed to R. Bieber, nine Cobble Yard. The clerk remembers the customer because he did not say a word, not even good morning.
leads.failureText: The counter clerk has been asked for other people’s post before and has a speech about it, which you hear twice.

leads.label: Ask along Cobble Yard about the clerk at number nine
leads.description: A yard that size knows who has been to work and who has not.
leads.successText: Six days off work, a parcel signed for, and a landlady who will talk to you on the step and not one stair higher.
leads.failureText: Cobble Yard has decided you are from the parish and closes like a fist.

leads.label: Put a price about for the notebook, and see who answers
leads.description: Quill of Alzuhod never handles the goods and never signs anything, which makes him worth exactly one conversation.
leads.successText: Somebody is bidding against you before you have finished naming the book, for a client described only by his manners — and a man in white face paint has been on the Tussock twice this week.
leads.failureText: Word goes out and comes back with your own price attached to it, which tells the whole market you want it and tells you nothing.

leads.label: Ask Hanass who consigned the notebook
leads.description: He sold it in May for four pounds. Somebody gave it to him to sell.
leads.successText: The price, the date, and the weather. On the consignor he becomes very interested in a shelf, and you notice that he has stopped keeping the shop after dark.
leads.failureText: He is sorry about your friend, sorrier about his stock, and has an appointment.

leads.label: Read the transcription the way it was meant to be read
leads.description: The bound copy McGovern made, in a language you have been able to read for eight days and never learned.
leads.successText: You get four pages in before the room gets colder than the evening accounts for, and you put it down, and the last thing you read is still there behind your eyes when you look away.
leads.failureText: The words hold still on the page and mean nothing, which is the only mercy this book has ever done anybody.
